lines.text: In 2025, nearly 1 in 3 US adults (30%) had income that varied at least occasionally.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-five, almost a third of US adults had income vary.

lines.text: 11% of all adults said that made bills hard to pay, up from about 9% in 2021.
lines.say: Eleven percent of all adults said that made bills hard to pay, up from about nine percent in twenty twenty-one.

lines.text: In a 2019 JPMorgan Chase Institute study of Chase data, the typical family's income changed 36% month to month.
lines.say: In a twenty nineteen JPMorgan Chase Institute study of Chase data, the typical family's income changed thirty-six percent month to month.

lines.text: Example: a made-up freelancer earns $2,600 to $5,000 monthly, averaging $3,600.
lines.say: Take a made-up freelancer earning two thousand six hundred to five thousand dollars monthly, averaging three thousand six hundred.

lines.text: One approach, baseline budgeting, plans essentials around the lowest month: $2,600.
lines.say: One approach, baseline budgeting, plans essentials around the lowest month, two thousand six hundred.

lines.text: Some add a buffer. In the $5,000 month, the $2,400 above baseline goes to a holding account.
lines.say: Some add a buffer. In the five thousand dollar month, the two thousand four hundred above baseline goes to a holding account.

lines.text: Others use percentages. Saving 20% is $520 in a low month and $1,000 in a high one.
lines.say: Others use percentages. Saving twenty percent is five hundred twenty dollars in a low month and one thousand in a high one.

lines.text: All three are ways to keep a low month from breaking the budget.
lines.say: All three are ways to keep a low month from breaking the budget.

post.title: 30% saw income vary in 2025. How people budget for it
post.ig:
In 2025, nearly 1 in 3 US adults had income that varied at least occasionally.

11% of all adults said that made bills hard to pay, up from about 9% in 2021 (Fed SHED).
A 2019 JPMorgan Chase Institute study found the typical family in its data (Chase accounts, 2013-2018) saw income move 36% month to month.
Three common approaches: baseline (lowest-month) budgeting, an income buffer, and percent-based allocation. Hypothetical example inside.

Sources: Federal Reserve, Economic Well-Being of U.S. Households in 2025 (May 2026); JPMorgan Chase Institute, Weathering Volatility 2.0 (Oct 2019).
News and education, not financial advice.
